title: Assessment and Verification

blocks.text: Assess whether the patient's defect type is femoral or tibial to determine the augment selection and
confirm the surgical plan.
Prosthesis parameters include: 9mm for the distal and posterior femoral condyle, 5mm for the tibial
plateau, and a minimum insert thickness of 6mm.
The required minimum gap space is 20mm.
Use gap spacer blocks to measure both flexion and extension gaps, and decide whether to address the
defect through tibial augmentation, femoral distal augmentation, and/or posterior femoral augmentation.

title: Tibial Reaming Procedure

blocks.text: The reamers range from 9mm to 18mm in diameter, increasing in 1mm increments. Reaming is performed
using a T-handle wrench, and the process must be conducted step by step until cortical contact is
achieved.
During reaming, pay close attention to the depth of the reamer. Depth markers (120, 160, 220) are indicat-
ed on the reamer shaft.
Note: If a 120mm extension stem is used on the tibial side, the total length consists of the extension stem
+ offset connector + tibial plateau length.
(The keel + offset connector combined length is 55mm.)
Assuming the extension stem has a length of 120mm

title: Insert the Tibial Extension Trial Stem

blocks.text: Select the extension trial stem corresponding to the final reamer size, and insert it into the medullary cavity
using the T-handle wrench to the predetermined reaming depth.
Note: The extension trial stem may fit slightly tightly to ensure stability during subsequent procedures.

title: Tibial Plateau Osteotomy And Trimming

blocks.text: Assemble the intramedullary osteotomy height locator with the tibial cutting block and insert it into the
extension trial stem.  The height and position of the cutting block can be adjusted using a crab clamp or a
0mm osteotomy calibration pin.
After securing the cutting block, loosen the anterior and posterior knobs, remove the cutting block holder,
and finally extract the intramedullary positioning
Perform the osteotomy. (The purpose of the osteotomy is
to create a uniform planar surface. If bone defects are
present, the current protocol requires defect confirmation
and subsequent osteotomy after installing the tibial trial
prosthesis.)

title: Tibial Plateau Eccentricity Verification

blocks.text: Select the appropriate tibial drill guide paired with a +0 offset adjuster, then assess the anteroposterior
and mediolateral positioning of the tibial plateau to choose the correct size.
If the size is appropriate but coverage is insufficient, adjust the coverage using +2, +4, or +6 offset adjust-
ers. Once optimal coverage is confirmed, record the position of the offset indicator and mark the reference
line with an electrocautery pen or similar tool.
The offset indicator scale ranges from 1 to 12. Positions may be clinically documented as Position 3、
Between 3 and 4、3 leaning toward 4(or similar descriptive notations).
Remove the tibial drill guide and offset adjuster,
while leaving the extension trial stem within the
medullary cavity.

text:
Select the appropriate tibial drill guide paired with a +0 offset adjuster, then assess the anteroposterior and mediolateral positioning of the tibial plateau to choose the correct size.

If the size is appropriate but coverage is insufficient, adjust the coverage using +2, +4, or +6 offset adjusters. Once optimal coverage is confirmed, record the position of the offset indicator and mark the reference line with an electrocautery pen or similar tool. The offset indicator scale ranges from 1 to 12. Positions may be clinically documented as Position 3、 Between 3 and 4、3 leaning toward 4(or similar descriptive notations).

Remove the tibial drill guide and offset adjuster, while leaving the extension trial stem within the medullary cavity.

title: Assemble The Tibial Plateau Component

blocks.text: Select the extension trial stem matching the diameter and length of the reamer used clinically, along with
the tibial plateau trial prosthesis and the offset connector trial. Based on the recorded position of the
offset indicator, use a hex wrench to adjust the relative alignment between the offset connector and the
reference mark on the anterior edge of the tibial plateau trial.
Note: If an offset connector is not required, the extension stem may be directly attached to the trial
prosthesis.

title: Tibial Keel Preparation

blocks.text: Confirm the reaming procedure based on whether an offset connector is selected.
Scenario 1: With Offset Connector  Assemble the offset reamer and reamer buckle with the indicator arrow
facing downward.
Perform the first reaming by adjusting the reamer
buckle to the "TIBIA" position, then ream along the
direction of the extension trial stem.
For the second reaming, attach the tibial drill
guide with the offset adjuster to the tibial plateau,
adjust it to the selected offset connector and its
indicated position, and secure it with fixation pins.
Remove the offset indicator and extract the extension trial stem.
Install the tibial depth gauge onto the tibial drill guide, ensure the reamer buckle is adjusted to the "TIBIA"
position, and proceed with reaming.
Scenario 2: Without Offset Connector  Assemble the offset reamer and reamer buckle with the indicator
arrow facing downward.
Perform the first reaming by adjusting the reamer buckle to the "T" position, then ream along the direction
of the extension trial stem.
Note: If no offset connector is used, proceed with reaming the tibial keel directly.

title: Tibial Plateau Trial Implantation

blocks.text: Verify the specifications of the tibial plateau trial, the offset magnitude and position of the offset connec-
tor, and the length and diameter of the extension trial stem.   Once confirmed, proceed with the complete
implantation of the tibial trial assembly. After implantation, use an electrocautery pen to mark and confirm
the positioning.
Use the keel rasp to trim and shape the tibial plateau keel.

blocks.text: After rotating the tail end of the connection handle, attach it to the tibial cutting guide and mount the
assembly onto the tibial tray trial for implantation.   Temporarily secure the tibial cutting guide to the
proximal tibia using screws for auxiliary fixation. Proceed with transverse osteotomy directly, then remove
the prosthesis to perform longitudinal osteotomy.
After completing the osteotomy, select the tibial
defect trial corresponding to the affected side,
attach it to the tibial trial prosthesis, and
implant the assembly.

title: Femoral Condyle Size Assessment

blocks.text: Option 1: Use the femoral condyle measuring plate to confirm the anteroposterior (AP) dimension of the
femoral condyle, and assist in assessing distal and posterior condylar defects.
Option 2: Use the femoral condyle trial prosthesis
(requires removal of the intercondylar notch), the
4-in-1 cutting block, or the ML measuring scale to
confirm the mediolateral (ML) dimension of the
femoral condyle and assist in determining its size.

title: Femoral Reaming Procedure

blocks.text: The reamers range from 9mm to 18mm in diameter, increasing in 1mm increments. Reaming is performed
using a T-handle wrench and must be conducted step by step until cortical contact is achieved. During
reaming, pay close attention to the depth of the reamer. Depth markers (120mm, 160mm, 220mm) are
indicated on the reamer shaft.
Note: For the femoral side, if a 120mm extension stem is used, the total length is calculated as:   Extension
stem + femoral condyle prosthesis length.   (The offset connector has a length of 30mm.)   If a 120mm
extension stem combined with an offset connector is used, the reaming depth must reach 150mm.

title: Femoral Condyle Distal Trimming

blocks.text: Install the femoral distal cutting guide, cutting guide plate, and femoral offset guide. Use a crab clamp to
assist in assessing distal femoral defects, and adjust the distal femoral condyle osteotomy thickness using
+5mm, +10mm, or +15mm augment options.
The femoral offset guide is marked with "LATERAL" (indicating the lateral side of the femur).
After confirming the osteotomy, secure the femoral cutting guide with fixation pins, then sequentially
remove the femoral offset guide and the distal cutting guide.

text:
Install the femoral distal cutting guide, cutting guide plate, and femoral offset guide. Use a crab clamp to assist in assessing distal femoral defects, and adjust the distal femoral condyle osteotomy thickness using +5mm, +10mm, or +15mm augment options. The femoral offset guide is marked with "LATERAL" (indicating the lateral side of the femur).

After confirming the osteotomy, secure the femoral cutting guide with fixation pins, then sequentially remove the femoral offset guide and the distal cutting guide.

title: Femoral Condyle 4-in-1 Position Verification

blocks.text: This demonstration illustrates the management of distal femoral defects.   Select the appropriate 4-in-1
cutting block size by verifying its fit in both superior-inferior and mediolateral dimensions to determine
the optimal specification.
Choose the femoral defect augment matching the selected size and thickness, and mount it onto the 4-
in-1 cutting block (note: it cannot be locked at this stage and may dislodge if mishandled). Install the
femoral offset guide and confirm the positioning of the 4-in-1 assembly
The offset guide offers four distinct offset options. Rotate the offset indicator dial to confirm and record
the selected offset position.
Femoral Offset Reference: Clock Method.

title: Assemble Femoral Condyle Prosthesis

blocks.text: Verify the specifications of the femoral condyle trial, the offset magnitude and position of the offset
connector, and the length and diameter of the extension trial stem.
Disassemble the intercondylar notch of the femoral condyle trial, then assemble the femoral condyle guide
rod with the offset connector and the extension trial stem.
Based on clinical requirements, install the trial augments for the distal femoral defect and posterior
condylar defect onto the femoral condyle trial. Adjust the offset magnitude and position of the offset
connector. The offset indicator line is located on the lateral side of the femoral condyle.

The femoral condyle eccentric alignment line is 
oriented toward the left side of the condyle.

title: Prosthesis Range of Motion Test

blocks.text: Mount the complete femoral condyle trial and tibial plateau trial onto the femoral and tibial bones, respec-
tively.  The meniscal insert size corresponds to the femoral condyle size, and it can only differ by one size
from the tibial plateau.  Place the meniscal insert trial between the knee prosthesis components and verify
the range of motion through flexion and extension testing.

title: Instrument Handling Precautions

blocks.text: 1. The femoral condyle trial prosthesis and offset guide trial
each have only one screw.
2. The offset trial contains an internal screw that requires
critical inspection prior to operation.
There is a small screw—do not unscrew it.
3. Quantity of Extension Trial Stems:
• 80mm: 3 units
• 120mm: 10 units (excluding 17mm and 19mm diameters)
• 160mm: 10 units (excluding 17mm and 19mm diameters)
4. Quantity of Tibial Defect Augments:
• 5 sizes × 3 thicknesses × bilateral sides = 30 units
5. Quantity of Femoral Defect Augments:
• Distal Augments: 5 sizes × 3 thicknesses × 2 identical sets = 30 units
• Posterior Condylar Augments: 5 sizes × 2 thicknesses × 2 identical sets = 20 units
6. Quantity of 4-in-1 Defect Auxiliary Augments:
• 5 sizes × 3 thicknesses × 2 identical sets = 30 units
7. Current Trial Stem Availability:
• Only one set each for 120mm and 160mm trial stems (planned to increase 120mm to two sets).
• During use, if the same size is required for both tibial and femoral applications, a one-size-smaller
diameter may be substituted.

title: Prosthesis Handling Precautions

blocks.text: 1. Prosthesis Inventory Requirements:
• Extension stems:
• 120mm: 2 sets
• 80mm: 1 set
• 160mm: 1 set
• Femoral defect augments:
• Distal augments (5mm, 10mm): 2 sets each
• Posterior condylar augments (5mm): 2 sets
• Offset connectors: 2 sets
2. Prosthesis Removal Notes:
• The femoral condyle prosthesis and tibial plateau prosthesis each contain two small screws. Avoid
dropping them during handling.
• Recommended procedure: Partially disengage the prosthesis first, then slowly remove the screws.
• Both screws must be reinserted during assembly. Avoid over-tightening to prevent thread stripping.
3. Prosthesis Installation Notes:
• Extension Stem Alignment: The orientation of the extension stem fork may be determined clinical-
ly(non-mandatory reference).
• Tibial Side Installation: The tibial component must be oriented with mediolateral opening to release
stress from varus/valgus forces, particularly critical for CCK (Condylar Constrained Knee) prostheses.
• Femoral Side Installation: The femoral component must be oriented with anteroposterior opening to
accommodate femoral anterior bowing and mitigate stress during flexion-extension movement.
